title: Yara and the Landfall
premise: Rosalind Joubert, a salvage diver who has spent a decade outrunning her family's disgraced name, takes a contract on a wreck the navy quietly forbids anyone to discuss. When an unusual tide exposes a sea cave beneath the cliffs, she finds evidence that the wreck is tied to her own inheritance—and to the coastal community she's always refused to call home. Racing the salvage fleet and expiring concession permits, Rosalind has six tides to prove the wreck belongs to the town, not the company, while falling for the harbor master sworn to enforce the rules against her. She wins the claim at cost of her anonymity, chooses to stay, and finally lets herself belong.
about_author: Astrid Fairweather grew up in a fishing village on the North Atlantic coast, where she learned to read tides before she learned to read maps. A former marine surveyor, she now writes adventure novels about people who can't stop moving until they learn why they should.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Diving a charted-but-denied wreck off Greyhaven Point, she recovers a brass fitting stamped with her family crest and hides it from her crew. The emotional beat is unease: the past she fled has surfaced in her hands, and she decides to investigate alone rather than walk away as instinct demands.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Harbor master Elias Vane serves her the concession notice: permits expire in six tides, and the Marrow & Finch salvage fleet arrives after. Their antagonism crackles into reluctant respect when he recognizes her surname and says nothing. The beat is wary alliance—two people bound by duty they resent.

chapters.title: What the Low Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. An extreme low tide reveals a cave mouth below the cliffs; inside she finds a sealed diver's chest belonging to her grandfather, lost decades ago on this same wreck. Reading his logbook, she learns he was framed for the disaster that ruined the Joubert name. The beat is grief transmuting into purpose.

chapters.title: The Town That Remembers
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias navigates Greyhaven's politics: old-timers who still curse the Jouberts, a councilman secretly negotiating with Marrow & Finch, and his own orders to keep Rosalind off the site. He begins bending rules for her. The beat is divided loyalty—duty pulling one way, conscience the other.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Racing the clock, Rosalind dives the wreck by night with Elias running surface cover, recovering documents proving the cargo was misdeclared—a navy cover-up implicating the company that now claims it. Caught in a squall, they nearly lose the boat and each other. The beat is trust forged under pressure, love edging past denial.

chapters.title: Marrow & Finch Arrives
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The fleet anchors early, permits be damned, led by surveyor Callum Reyes—an old partner who knows Rosalind's real identity and offers her a cut to stand down. She refuses; he threatens to expose her falsified dive certifications. The beat is fear and defiance: staying invisible was never really an option.

chapters.title: The Cave Claim
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias discovers the councilman sold the concession illegally and confronts him, losing his job for it. Meanwhile Rosalind files an adverse claim through the cave—her grandfather's original survey, hidden in the chest, predates every permit. The beat is sacrifice: both abandon the safety of their positions for what's right.

chapters.title: Storm Tide
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. With two tides left, a storm seals the cave and Marrow & Finch begins salvage anyway. Rosalind dives in dangerous surge to reach the captain's strongroom—the final proof—while Elias holds off the fleet's tender in the harbor launch. The beat is terror and resolve; she nearly drowns choosing the truth over survival.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At the emergency admiralty hearing, Callum exposes Rosalind's record, but her grandfather's survey, the recovered manifests, and testimony from Greyhaven's oldest families outweigh it. The wreck and cave are awarded to the town in perpetuity; Marrow & Finch withdraws. The beat is vindication shadowed by loss—Rosalind may face charges and exile.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Facing a suspended sentence and a stripped certification, Rosalind expects to run again—but the town offers her work restoring the wreck as a heritage site, and Elias offers something quieter. She signs the papers, hangs her grandfather's compass in the harbor office, and stays. The beat is homecoming: belonging chosen, not inherited.
